source_text: Counterarguments prioritized empirical evidence of harm, emphasizing that FGM—typically performed on girls under 15 without anesthesia—involves partial or total excision of external genitalia, leading to immediate risks like severe bleeding, infection, and shock, alongside long-term consequences including chronic pain, urinary and menstrual disorders, obstetric complications (e.g., increased cesarean needs and perinatal mortality), and psychological trauma such as depression and post-traumatic stress. [9]
